12 A shop sign weighing 75 N hangs from a frame attached to a vertical wall.
Z
30°
Y
X
0.50 m
wall
sign
weight 75 N
The frame consists of a horizontal rod XY and a rod YZ that is at an angle of 30° to the horizontal.
Rod XY is attached to the wall by a hinge at X and has length 0.50 m. Assume that the weights of
the rods are negligible.
What is the horizontal force exerted by the wall on rod XY?
A
0 N
B
43 N
C
130 N
D
150 N

hints: Notice the $75 \text{ N}$ sign acts vertically down at Y, $0.50 \text{ m}$ from the hinge at X, while rod YZ pulls at Y at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.
For rod XY in equilibrium, take moments about the hinge X so the unknown hinge forces have no moment and only the $75 \text{ N}$ weight and the vertical component of the YZ force matter.
Once the force in YZ is found, resolve it horizontally with $\cos 30^{\circ}$ and use horizontal force balance on XY to find the wall force at X.
walkthrough: Consider rod XY alone. At Y it carries the $75 \text{ N}$ weight down and the force $T$ from rod YZ directed toward Z, at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal to the left.
Take moments about hinge X for XY. The hinge forces have zero moment about X. The clockwise moment is $75 \text{ N} \times 0.50 \text{ m}$.
The anticlockwise moment is only from the vertical component of $T$, which is $T\sin 30^{\circ}$, with perpendicular distance $0.50 \text{ m}$. So $T\sin 30^{\circ} \times 0.50 = 75 \times 0.50$.
Hence $T = 75 / \sin 30^{\circ} = 75 / 0.5 = 150 \text{ N}$. This is the force in YZ.
For horizontal equilibrium of XY, the wall force $F$ at X must balance the horizontal component of $T$ at Y, which pulls left with $T\cos 30^{\circ}$.
So $F = T\cos 30^{\circ} = 150 \times \cos 30^{\circ} \approx 150 \times 0.866 \approx 130 \text{ N}$ to the right. This is option C.

A.explanation: A hinge at X must push horizontally to balance the horizontal pull from rod YZ at Y, so the horizontal force cannot be zero.

B.explanation: About $43 \text{ N}$ is $75 \tan 30^{\circ}$, which confuses which trigonometric component of the YZ force provides the upward support.

C.explanation: Moment equilibrium about X gives $T = 150 \text{ N}$ in YZ, whose horizontal component $T\cos 30^{\circ} \approx 130 \text{ N}$ must be balanced by the wall on XY.

D.explanation: $150 \text{ N}$ is the full force in rod YZ, not its horizontal component acting on XY.
